findings.reason: a worker either stops on an out-of-scope edit or races §3 on a shared file, and the plan's claim that the four sections are disjoint is false as written; §5 needs `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py` added to its write paths (or the marking moved to a §3 deliverable) and the followup corrected.
findings.text: §5 states that `_request_host_follower` sets `owner_checked: true` on the request line, but that function lives in `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:818`, which is §3's write path and absent from §5's five declared write paths, so a §5 worker cannot make the change it is told to make, and a §3 worker running concurrently (as the followup's "disjoint files … can run together" invites) would land `_request_host_follower` without the field §5 then depends on

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — at base ea60b2749f every §5 anchor resolves: `crew-host` wait loop and exec at lines 47–67, `crew_host` at `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2774`, `run` at `reckon/crew/session_host.py:710`, `record()` at `:368`, `_remove_fifo` at `:615`, `supervise` record write at `:667`, `_TERMINAL_RUN_PHASES` at `reckon/crew/node.py:33`, `LAUNCH_FAILED_PHASE` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:101`, the launch-failed-as-failed read at `reckon/crew/runs.py:2275`, `_pointer_session` at `reckon/crew/resumption.py:753`, `_hand_off_to_waiting_host` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:870`; and §5's reference to the nova-8a session `35a66cc6` on nova-39's host resolves in §1.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of §5's six cases is a measurable assertion, and the sixth (FIFO removal, which passes at base by design) carries its own negative control, so no case is unfalsifiable.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5 places every log under the run directory, a durable crew path, not a scratchpad or node-local temporary tree.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `owner_checked` and `waiting_for_dispatch` name what they carry; no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose enter the code they describe.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §5's root cause is the script's own pre-exec wait, which the cited lines 47–67 show; the scan, the accept set and the record field are each capable of producing the six cases as written; and the mechanism runs on the real path, naming the plugin script exec into `crew_host` and then `session_host.run`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 delivers one outcome (a re-armed host adopts its owner's live runs and records that it is waiting when there are none); the script, the scan and the record field are all necessary to it.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5's new `owner_checked` marking is set inside `_request_host_follower` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:818`), a file §3 owns and §5's write paths do not list, while the plan's only open followup says the four sections "write disjoint files and can run together".
